questions.question: Define a market and distinguish between factor markets and goods and services markets, giving one example of each. Explain how they are linked in the circular flow.
questions.expected_answer: A market is any arrangement that brings buyers and sellers together to exchange at a price (no building needed). Factor markets: households sell factors of production to businesses (e.g. labour market, financial market). Goods and services markets: businesses sell final products to households (e.g. bread, haircuts). Households earn rent, wages, interest and profit in factor markets and spend that income in goods and services markets; businesses use sales revenue to pay for factors again.

questions.question: Describe the labour market: who supplies and who demands labour, the price of labour, and the role of trade unions, government and the CCMA. Give two causes of unemployment in South Africa.
questions.expected_answer: Supply: households/workers; demand: employers (derived from demand for products); price: wages and salaries. Trade unions bargain collectively for workers; government sets labour laws (LRA 1995, BCEA 1997, National Minimum Wage Act 2018, Employment Equity Act) and runs the UIF; the CCMA settles disputes. Causes: slow economic growth; skills mismatch; legacy of apartheid education and spatial planning; transport costs to jobs.

questions.question: The bakery borrows R120 000 for a new oven at 12% per year. Calculate the interest for one year, state whether this is a money market or capital market transaction, and explain the role of the bank as an intermediary.
questions.expected_answer: Interest = 12% × 120 000 = R14 400 (total repaid R134 400 if repaid after one year). Capital market: long-term finance (more than one year) for equipment. The bank collects deposits from many savers, pays them a lower rate (e.g. 5%), lends to borrowers at a higher rate, assesses risk and spreads it; the interest margin covers costs and profit.
